hero.headline: Arrest report details threats, gunfire that led to Palm City SWAT standoff
hero.teaser: A newly released arrest report reveals Darrel Abbey threatened to kill his ex-girlfriend and her stepfather, fired shots at a bucket hanging from a tree, and attempted to wipe away evidence before the hours-long SWAT standoff in Palm City on Saturday.
hero.body:
Darrel Abbey, 38, of Palm City threatened to kill his ex-girlfriend and her stepfather, fired shots outside his home, and attempted to destroy evidence before barricading himself in a guest house during an hours-long SWAT standoff with the Martin County Sheriff's Office on Saturday. A newly released arrest report provides detailed accounts of the incident on Southwest Bessey Creek Trail near Murphy Road that began when Abbey's ex-girlfriend arrived at his home at about 12:08 p.m. after the two had broken up the previous night.

 According to the arrest report, Abbey was extremely intoxicated and armed with a rifle he kept in his Tesla and a 10 mm handgun in his shorts when the woman arrived. She told investigators Abbey was not doing well mentally and had previously made comments about killing himself. The report says Abbey brought both firearms inside and began screaming at the woman while holding a gun, pointing it at her several times and threatening to kill her and her stepfather.

 Investigators said Abbey at one point placed the gun under his chin and pulled the trigger, but the firearm did not discharge because the magazine had been removed. Abbey continued drinking bourbon and Jameson throughout the encounter and later walked outside where the woman heard several loud sounds. He returned to retrieve a rifle and allegedly tried to get the woman to come outside and shoot with him, telling her he had hung a bucket from a nearby tree and was shooting at it.

 The report says Abbey later began cleaning the firearms and said he had to wipe all his fingerprints off and get the gunshot residue off his hands because he was not going back to prison. Abbey attempted to get into his vehicle while continuing to drink, prompting the woman to begin recording him. When Abbey realized she was recording, he allegedly reached for her phone and she ran down the road until a passing motorist stopped to help her.

 Deputies later attempted to contact Abbey at the residence, but he refused to open the door or speak with them, leading to the standoff involving the SWAT team and hostage negotiators. Abbey was booked into the Martin County Jail without bond on charges including battery and aggravated assault with a deadly weapon without intent to kill. Investigators said Abbey is a convicted felon from Washington state with a prior conviction for vehicular assault.

cards.headline: Man shot at Port St. Lucie Pollo Tropical charged as aggressor in confrontation
cards.teaser: Christopher Harris, who was shot outside a Pollo Tropical restaurant in Port St. Lucie on September 19, now faces criminal charges after police determined he was the primary aggressor in the confrontation.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie police have charged Christopher Harris, 37, after determining he was the primary aggressor in a September 19 confrontation outside a Pollo Tropical restaurant on NW St. Lucie West Boulevard that ended with him being shot. Harris faces attempted aggravated battery with a deadly weapon and felony battery charges, while the shooter faces no criminal charges. The incident prompted a heavy law enforcement response Saturday evening, with crime scene tape surrounding the restaurant and multiple officers investigating as a subject was taken into custody at the scene.

 Officers responded around 3:43 p.m. September 19 to the restaurant at 1365 NW St. Lucie West Boulevard and found Harris suffering from a gunshot wound to his upper torso. He was flown to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital with non-life-threatening injuries.

 Isaiah Davis, 25, was detained at the scene while detectives investigated. Officers recovered a firearm.

 Surveillance video showed Harris following Davis inside the restaurant despite not appearing to place or pick up an order, police said. Davis had entered to pick up a food delivery order. Exterior surveillance showed Harris pushing Davis and advancing toward him as Davis moved backward.

 Investigators said Harris was armed with a knife during the confrontation, and witnesses reported seeing him with a knife shortly before the shooting. Davis fired one round, striking Harris in the chest.

 Harris went back inside the restaurant, where people provided aid and called 911. One knife was recovered after it had been removed from Harris's waistband while people were helping him, police said. Another knife was later found in his front pocket.

 After reviewing surveillance video, physical evidence and witness statements, detectives determined Harris was the primary aggressor and established probable cause for the charges. The felony battery charge is based on a prior battery conviction. Police said an arrest affidavit was submitted to the St. Lucie County jail. Harris is expected to be booked after he is medically released from the hospital.

cards.headline: Charter bus fire closed I-95 southbound lanes in Hobe Sound; driver escaped unharmed
cards.teaser: A charter bus caught fire Monday morning on I-95 in Martin County, closing all southbound lanes and snarling traffic. The driver, who was alone on the bus, escaped without injury.
cards.body:
A charter bus caught fire Monday morning on Interstate 95 in Martin County, prompting authorities to close all southbound lanes and launch an investigation into the cause.

 The fire occurred around 11:20 a.m. on the southbound side of the interstate. Martin County Fire Rescue responded to the scene to extinguish the blaze.

 The driver was the only person on the bus at the time of the fire and was able to escape the vehicle. No injuries were reported in the incident.

 One southbound lane of I-95 has since reopened to traffic. Authorities continue to investigate what caused the charter bus to catch fire.

cards.headline: Molly's House open house Monday marks 30 years helping Treasure Coast families
cards.teaser: Molly's House is hosting an open house Monday at its facility on Osceola Street in Stuart, inviting community members to tour the house and healing garden while marking 30 years of
cards.body:
Molly's House is hosting an open house Monday at its facility on Osceola Street in Stuart, inviting community members to tour the house and healing garden while marking 30 years of providing affordable lodging and support services for patients and families receiving medical treatment on the Treasure Coast.

 The nonprofit organization, located in Stuart's medical district, was founded to help families stay close to doctors, hospitals and treatment providers during difficult medical situations. The mission focuses on reducing stress for families facing long-term care and recovery.

 Kate Wiegerink, a member of the Molly's House board of directors and Molly Sharkey's sister, said the organization works to educate new doctors, nurses and community members about the services available to patients and families. Molly's House provides affordable lodging for guests traveling for treatment and offers a free cancer support program for residents.

 Brandi Patricio, whose son TJ is receiving treatment, said having access to affordable lodging reduces anxiety about housing costs during treatment and allows families to focus on recovery and care. Molly's House provides weekly free meals to residents to help ease food expenses and preparation during stressful medical situations. Businesses and individuals can become a "Chef for a Day" and provide an average of 28 meals.

 Organization leaders said demand for support services remains strong as more families seek affordable options near treatment centers across South Florida and the Treasure Coast.

hero.headline: Arrest report details threats, gunfire that led to Palm City SWAT standoff
hero.teaser: A newly released arrest report reveals Darrel Abbey threatened to kill his ex-girlfriend and her stepfather, fired shots at a bucket hanging from a tree, and attempted to wipe away evidence before the hours-long SWAT standoff in Palm City on Saturday.
hero.body:
Darrel Abbey, 38, of Palm City threatened to kill his ex-girlfriend and her stepfather, fired shots outside his home, and attempted to destroy evidence before barricading himself in a guest house during an hours-long SWAT standoff with the Martin County Sheriff's Office on Saturday. A newly released arrest report provides detailed accounts of the incident on Southwest Bessey Creek Trail near Murphy Road that began when Abbey's ex-girlfriend arrived at his home at about 12:08 p.m. after the two had broken up the previous night.

 According to the arrest report, Abbey was extremely intoxicated and armed with a rifle he kept in his Tesla and a 10 mm handgun in his shorts when the woman arrived. She told investigators Abbey was not doing well mentally and had previously made comments about killing himself. The report says Abbey brought both firearms inside and began screaming at the woman while holding a gun, pointing it at her several times and threatening to kill her and her stepfather.

 Investigators said Abbey at one point placed the gun under his chin and pulled the trigger, but the firearm did not discharge because the magazine had been removed. Abbey continued drinking bourbon and Jameson throughout the encounter and later walked outside where the woman heard several loud sounds. He returned to retrieve a rifle and allegedly tried to get the woman to come outside and shoot with him, telling her he had hung a bucket from a nearby tree and was shooting at it.

 The report says Abbey later began cleaning the firearms and said he had to wipe all his fingerprints off and get the gunshot residue off his hands because he was not going back to prison. Abbey attempted to get into his vehicle while continuing to drink, prompting the woman to begin recording him. When Abbey realized she was recording, he allegedly reached for her phone and she ran down the road until a passing motorist stopped to help her.

 Deputies later attempted to contact Abbey at the residence, but he refused to open the door or speak with them, leading to the standoff involving the SWAT team and hostage negotiators. Abbey was booked into the Martin County Jail without bond on charges including battery and aggravated assault with a deadly weapon without intent to kill. Investigators said Abbey is a convicted felon from Washington state with a prior conviction for vehicular assault.

cards.body:
A charter bus caught fire Monday morning on Interstate 95 in Martin County, prompting authorities to close all southbound lanes and launch an investigation into the cause.

 The fire occurred around 11:20 a.m. on the southbound side of the interstate. Martin County Fire Rescue responded to the scene to extinguish the blaze.

 The driver was the only person on the bus at the time of the fire and was able to escape the vehicle. No injuries were reported in the incident.

 One southbound lane of I-95 has since reopened to traffic. Authorities continue to investigate what caused the charter bus to catch fire.

hero.headline: Man shot at Port St. Lucie Pollo Tropical charged as aggressor in confrontation
hero.teaser: Christopher Harris, who was shot outside a Pollo Tropical restaurant in Port St. Lucie on September 19, now faces criminal charges after police determined he was the primary aggressor in the confrontation.
hero.body:
Port St. Lucie police have charged Christopher Harris, 37, after determining he was the primary aggressor in a September 19 confrontation outside a Pollo Tropical restaurant on NW St. Lucie West Boulevard that ended with him being shot. Harris faces attempted aggravated battery with a deadly weapon and felony battery charges, while the shooter faces no criminal charges. The incident prompted a heavy law enforcement response Saturday evening, with crime scene tape surrounding the restaurant and multiple officers investigating as a subject was taken into custody at the scene.

 Officers responded around 3:43 p.m. September 19 to the restaurant at 1365 NW St. Lucie West Boulevard and found Harris suffering from a gunshot wound to his upper torso. He was flown to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital with non-life-threatening injuries.

 Isaiah Davis, 25, was detained at the scene while detectives investigated. Officers recovered a firearm.

 Surveillance video showed Harris following Davis inside the restaurant despite not appearing to place or pick up an order, police said. Davis had entered to pick up a food delivery order. Exterior surveillance showed Harris pushing Davis and advancing toward him as Davis moved backward.

 Investigators said Harris was armed with a knife during the confrontation, and witnesses reported seeing him with a knife shortly before the shooting. Davis fired one round, striking Harris in the chest.

 Harris went back inside the restaurant, where people provided aid and called 911. One knife was recovered after it had been removed from Harris's waistband while people were helping him, police said. Another knife was later found in his front pocket.

 After reviewing surveillance video, physical evidence and witness statements, detectives determined Harris was the primary aggressor and established probable cause for the charges. The felony battery charge is based on a prior battery conviction. Police said an arrest affidavit was submitted to the St. Lucie County jail. Harris is expected to be booked after he is medically released from the hospital.
